payload.rationale: Inventory.snapshot() assigns the private self._stock dict to a local and returns it, so callers receive a reference to the inventory's real state; mutating the snapshot (e.g. snap["A"] = 100) writes directly into _stock and corrupts stock levels. Wrapping it in dict() returns a shallow copy, fulfilling the documented contract ('a copy of available stock per sku; callers may mutate it freely'). A shallow copy is sufficient because the values are immutable ints. This is the smallest change: it only adds the copy, leaving all other behavior (including available/reserve/release/restock/low_stock) untouched.
